## f0069f2752a4

**Reproduced shortcut / domain-coverage defect.** Generator v4.0.0, SHA-256
`009e060f7e413659268f1b82c406a6e5b970eb06dc07b62fc9af44f9a7db1e13`, never
emitted a surviving border-touching component larger than five cells in the
checked domain. The rival “keep border-touching components only when size ≤ 5”
matched all 3/3 canonical pairs and all 600/600 production samples (200 per band;
seeds `700000..700199`, `710000..710199`, `720000..720199`, sample indices
`0..199`). Canonical maximum survivor size was 4; sampled production maximum was 5.

A self-check-accepted 8×8 witness contains a six-cell 2×3 border component and one
interior singleton. The intended rule preserves all six border cells; the rival
erases them, differing in six cells. Selected Racket execution is valid, matches
the Python intended output, and differs from the rival. Exact evidence:
`checks/audit/f0069f2752a4/finding.json`, `input.json`, `rival.json`,
`python-intended.json`, `racket.json`, and `racket-comparison.json`.

Reproduction from packet root:

```bash
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply f0069f2752a4 \
  --input ../checks/audit/f0069f2752a4/input.json \
  --out ../checks/audit/f0069f2752a4/racket.json
```

The witness belongs to the validator-accepted task domain but not the current
finite production shape bank. This is a finite canonical/600-sample finding, not
a claim about every possible emitted seed. Audit target source was left unchanged.
